FAQ

Which countries are a part of EU?

There are 27 countries that are part of the EU. They are Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Ireland, Greece, Portugal, Spain, Austria, Finland, Sweden, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Bulgaria, Romania, and Croatia. [...] Some people refer to the partnership between Germany and France as the core of the European Union. Germany is the economic and population powerhouse of the European Union. France and Belgium usually provide much of the EU bureaucracy. While the center of EU political and economic life is in Brussels, Belgium, the EU parliament is in Strasbourg, France. These six core countries not only share direct borders but also suffered some of the worst fighting and damage from World War II.

European Union (EU), international organization comprising 27 European countries and governing common economic, social, and security policies. Originally confined to western Europe, the EU undertook a robust expansion into central and eastern Europe in the early 21st century. The EU’s members are Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, [...] The EU members are: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain and Sweden. The United Kingdom was a founding member but left the EU in 2020. [...] In 1951, six countries—Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, and West Germany—signed the Treaty of Paris, establishing the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) in 1952. The ECSC formed a free-trade area for key economic and military resources and established supranational institutions to manage it. Further international treaties and revisions eventually led to the EU's creation.
